sources.title: GEMS Prize evaluation metric and submission format
sources.how: fetch_page (the sandbox's own HTTP client is blocked for this host; fetch_page is not)

quotes.metric: DTI(alpha, beta) = TPw / (TPw + alpha*FPw + beta*FNw + epsilon), with alpha = 0.2 and beta = 0.8; triangular kernel k(d) = max(1 - d/R, 0) with R = 300 m; TPw = sum over truth pixels g of max over prediction pixels x with d(x,g) <= R of p(x) k(d); FPw = sum over prediction pixels with p > 0 of p(x) [1 - max over g of k(d)]; FNw = sum over truth pixels g of [1 - max over x with d <= R of p(x) k(d)].
quotes.format: A single-band GeoTIFF (.tif) or a .zip containing exactly one GeoTIFF, matching the CRS, shape and geotransform of the submission format; values are confidences in [0, 1]; cells outside the provided data extent must be null or NaN. EPSG:32611, 100 m grid, same bounds as the training data.
quotes.features: training_features.tif carries conductivity, depth to conductive base, detrended elevation and slope, dilatation, shear strain rate, second invariant of strain rate, isostatic gravity anomaly and its slope, reduced-to-the-pole magnetic anomaly, TMI, vertical and horizontal slope of TMI, top-of-crustal magnetic source depth, and earthquake density; 1m_DEM_links.csv lists the LiDAR tiles.

sources.used_for: vendored src/gems56/metric.py (alpha, beta, R, kernel), the [0,1]-and-null rules in submission_writer, band selection in corrections.load_fields

sources.title: DrivenData staff on whether known fault pixels count against a submission
sources.author: chrisk-dd (DrivenData Staff), 2026-09-16

quotes.masking: Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked / excluded from evaluation, so they do not count towards penalty terms.
quotes.final_round: The final round also masks existing faults; for scoring purposes it should not matter whether these known faults are included with predictions or not.

sources.used_for: the whole premise of this lane: a dot sitting on a catalogue pixel earns nothing, so a correction is only worth emitting if the evidence-defined trace is measurably elsewhere; and the emission rule's 'never on a catalogue pixel' constraint

sources.title: Sibling repo GEMSDOE54: prune experiment and holdout protocol
sources.how: git clone of the repository, read of the markdown files and of the referenced receipts
claims_used: A child submission of 37,654 dots (parent 40,199 dots, minus exactly the 2,545 dots within 2 px of a catalogue fault) scored 0.2778 against the parent's 0.2708, i.e. removing mass from the catalogue raised the score.
Their blocked holdout (gemsdoe54-segment-cv v2, 3,199 segments, 60,988 withheld positives) reported best arms at DTI 0.0483 [0.0424, 0.0541] and 0.0465 [0.0400, 0.0531] against a 0.0104 chance floor.
Their detection floor d_min = 0.0495 with paired MDE 0.0043-0.0121, so board gaps of a few thousandths are not resolvable locally.
sources.status: sibling-reported, not organizer-confirmed; used as prior evidence about mechanism, never as a score for this project

sources.title: LiDAR-derived 100 m scarp stack and 3 m pilot tiles: provenance chain
sources.how: fetched the json and the workflow run that produced it (https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE48/actions/runs/37565284104, source run 37561683197, commit 09bda8a9)
sources.notes: Underlying data are USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar, publicly redistributable; the 100 m stack is int16 decimetre-packed with nodata -32768, the 3 m tiles decode as z_m = 1000 + v/10 in EPSG:26911. Decoding was verified against the rasters themselves, not the metadata (IR-56-005).

sources.title: Learning a Embedding of Spatiotemporal Data for Weakly Supervised Learning (Mnih & Hinton, ICML 2012) - the registration/omission-tolerant loss the brief names
sources.notes: The brief requires any learned component to use a max-pooled / weakly-labelled loss of this family. This lane trained nothing: the negative verdict means no learned component was admissible, so the constraint is recorded rather than exercised. The reference is kept here because the emission rule's corridor aggregation is the non-learned analogue of the same idea (a line is judged by its pixels, and pixels are judged by their line).

sources.title: DrivenData GEMS Prize problem description (metric, format, rounds)

quotes.metric: TI(alpha,beta)=sum p g / (sum p g + alpha sum p(1-g) + beta sum (1-p) g); k(d)=max(1-d/R,0), R=300 m; alpha 0.2, beta 0.8
quotes.format: float32, single layer, 100 m, EPSG 32611, values between 0 and 1; data outside bounds null or nan
quotes.rounds: Initial Prize Round scored on private set; Final Prize Round rescored on expanded labels
